title: 4.1 Translations

icans: I can name a vector and its components.
I can translate a figure using a vector or a coordinate rule.
I can compose translations and write one rule for them.

vocab: a quantity that has both ____________ and magnitude, shown as an arrow
a ___________ that moves or changes a figure in some way
the original figure and the new figure after a _________________
a transformation that moves every point of a figure the same distance in the same ____________
a _________________ that preserves length and angle measure

blocks.p: Trace △ABC with A(−4, 1), B(−1, 3), C(−2, −1). Slide it 5 right and 2 down.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Vector notation: ⟨a, b⟩ means move a units horizontally and b units _______________.

blocks.stem: Name the vector from A(1, 2) to B(4, −1) in component form.
Translate △ABC by the vector ⟨5, −2⟩. Give the image’s vertices.
A translation maps (2, 5) to (−1, 9). Write the rule.

notes: Composition Theorem: the composition of two (or more) rigid motions is a _______________ motion.

blocks.stem: Translate by (x, y) → (x + 2, y), then by (x, y) → (x, y − 4). Write one rule, and find the image of (1, 1).
A robot moves from (0, 0) to (3, 2), then from (3, 2) to (1, 7). What single vector takes it from start to finish?
A translation maps (3, −1) to (−2, 4). Write the rule.

tickets.stem: Is a translation a rigid motion? Explain.
